description: This laboratory course accompanies RAPC-301 (Robot Programming and Control). Students learn the structure, components, and coordinate systems of industrial robots and their control mechanisms; develop and implement robot programs for basic and advanced industrial tasks such as pick-and-place, palletizing, and path planning; integrate sensors, vision systems, and external control devices (e.g. PLCs) with robots for adaptive automation; and analyze robot performance parameters such as trajectory accuracy, repeatability, and operational safety using real-time data and simulations.
experiments: To study robot architecture, coordinate systems, DOF, controller interface.
To practice joint, world, tool, and user frame jogging.
To calibrate TCP using 4-point and 6-point calibration methods.
To write basic motion programs using PTP commands.
To execute linear (LIN) and circular (CIRC) trajectories.
To control trajectory smoothing using blending zones.
To verify Forward Kinematics / Inverse Kinematics using software and physical robot.
To perform Pick-and-Place Programming with Grippers.
To perform Programming of End-Effector Control (Digital I/O).
To study Vision-Guided Robotics: Object Detection & Alignment based on camera coordinates.
To study Force/Torque Controlled Operations with an objective to implement compliant motion for surface-follow or insertion.
To study Path Optimization & Workspace Analysis to optimize cycle time, avoid singularities, map workspace.
To study PLC-Robot Integration using Industrial Protocols.
To study Safety Programming & Emergency Handling of industrial robot.
outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of robot configurations, kinematics, and control architectures.
Write, execute, and troubleshoot robot programs for industrial operations using teach pendants and offline simulators.
Integrate and interface robots with vision systems, sensors, and PLCs to perform coordinated tasks.
Evaluate robot motion characteristics and performance metrics through experiments and simulation tools.
